# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1501
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1501
- **Title**: perf(1498): session JSONL parsed-line cache — repeat window scans splice, not re-parse
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1498-jsonl-parse-cache` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +814
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:21:25Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +814
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:21:25Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1501
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1501
- **Title**: perf(1498): session JSONL parsed-line cache — repeat window scans splice, not re-parse
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1498-jsonl-parse-cache` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +814
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:21:25Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1501
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1501
- **Title**: perf(1498): session JSONL parsed-line cache — repeat window scans splice, not re-parse
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1498-jsonl-parse-cache` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +814
- **Deletions**: -60
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:21:25Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

Also, I need to think carefully about correctness issues in this cache implementation:

1. Freshness: `_noteParseCacheStamp` is called in `stat()`. Growth keeps entries (append-only). But is the file really append-only? The PR says `WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended` rewrite rule uses mtime move for same-size rewrites. But what about external edits that change the file while the reader is open? If the file grows AND existing bytes are rewritten simultaneously (size grows, mtime changes), cache entries would be stale. The append-only contract assumption — is it enforced anywhere? If a user edits the session JSONL file while the TUI is open (e.g. deletes some lines at the end but appends more, net growth), stale cache entries would serve wrong data. This is a correctness risk worth flagging. Actually the same "append-only" assumption is used by readForward resume, so it's an existing contract. But cache amplifies the impact: previously each read re-parsed and would see the edits; now it serves stale records. Same-size mtime move clears, but a same-size rewrite that also changes... hmm, same-size mtime move clears. Net-growth rewrites keep stale entries. This is a genuine issue, though arguably aligned with existing storage semantics. Severity: IMPORTANT perhaps.

2. `_parseCacheLookup` key: (offset, byteLength, shallow). A line at same offset+length with different content after a rewrite — cleared on shrink/same-size-mtime. But if a rewrite grows the file while changing a prefix line's content... append-only contract violation. OK.

3. In `_collectNewest`, the `resolved` list is shared but not mutated elsewhere. Actually `resolved[i] = entry;` then later `picked.add(entry)` — fine. But one subtle bug: on the reverse walk, when a miss line is reached and parsed, `_parseCacheStore(entry, false)` is called — stores. OK.

4. Byte accounting bug: `_parseCacheStore` and `_parseCacheStoreTorn` add `entry.bytes` to `_parseCacheBytesUsed` unconditionally, even when the key already exists in the map. Overwriting an existing key would double-count bytes. Could a store hit an existing key? In `_collectNewest`, a given line appears once per `lines` list (offsets unique per scan? lines from a scan are distinct lines, distinct offsets). But could two lines in one scan share offset? No. Could the same key be stored twice within one scan from different code paths? `_parseCacheStore` is only called once per miss. But across scans: a miss line is not in cache, so store is a fresh insert. Hmm — unless the line was evicted between probe and store... probe said miss, then eviction... within one `_collectNewest` call, stores happen during the walk; a store could evict an entry that another later line in the same scan probed as miss? No — probes happen upfront before any store. Wait, order: probe loop first (all lines), then walk stores. So a line probed as miss, but between probe and store, could its key be inserted by... only this same walk inserts it. Each miss line inserted once. So no double insert. BUT: `_evictParseCache` could evict the entry just stored? `while (length > entries || bytesUsed > bytes)` — if exactly at cap, a new insert makes length cap+1, evicts the oldest (FIFO) — could evict the just-inserted one if map has... it removes keys.first — insertion order, the just-inserted is last, so it evicts older ones. Fine.

However — there IS a double-count scenario: `_parseCacheBytesUsed -= first.$2` on evict uses `first.$2` = byteLength. For torn marker, they added `bytes` (the raw line length). And `entry.bytes` for parsed entries. Consistent: `_parseCacheBytesUsed` sums raw line lengths. On re-store of existing key — I argued it can't happen within the invariants. Actually wait: can `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` be called concurrently? The reader's methods are async; if two scans interleave (async gaps), one scan probes miss for a line, awaits `parseBatch` (yield), another scan parses the same line and stores it; then first scan stores again → key overwritten, bytes double-counted, and `_parseCache.length` unchanged but bytesUsed inflated → premature eviction. Minor memory-accounting issue, requires concurrent scans on the same reader. Does the code allow concurrent calls? jumpToOffset/readTail etc. could be invoked concurrently from the TUI? Possibly. Even so, impact is bounded memory accounting inflation → early eviction, not incorrect data. And FIFO order on re-insertion: re-inserting an existing key in Dart's default LinkedHashMap preserves original insertion position (updating value doesn't move key). So the FIFO ordering assumption "Insertion order drives the FIFO eviction" holds for updates.

Another subtle one: `_parseCacheStoreTorn` when the key already exists as an entry? Same concurrency caveat.

5. Bigger correctness question in `_collectNewest`: the cap checks. Old code: `if (picked.length >= maxRecords) return ...` inside per-record loop, and `totalBytes >= maxBytes` check. New code: same checks but `break` instead of `return`, plus `torn[i] = true; continue` skips. Wait — there's a behavior change: old code parsed batches from newest and broke early. New code still walks newest-first (`i` from lines.length-1 down). Fine.

But there's a subtle difference: old code checked `picked.length >= maxRecords` at the top of each record iteration including before processing; new code checks at top of loop with `break`. Equivalent.

Another subtlety: the old code computed `totalBytes += weight + 1` only for non-null records. New code same.

6. `_decodeLines` on misses: the comment in `_parseAllLines` — "Full-parse semantics: every miss below is decoded + parsed now. `_parseCacheMisses += missIdx.length;`" but some misses may be undecodable (decoded list smaller than missIdx) — counters: miss counted even if decode fails; acceptable-ish. But worse: in `_parseAllLines`, misses that failed to decode (j<0 equivalent) — they build `lineIdxByOffset` only for offsets present in decoded; lines not decoded are silently skipped (remain null in results, not stored as torn!). Old code: lines that fail decode are just skipped too. But new code fails to store them as torn, so re-scans will re-probe miss and re-attempt decode — only a perf nit, plus miss counter semantics. Hmm wait, actually does `_decodeLines` drop lines? Let me check its implementation. Also, misses counted upfront for all missIdx even if the walk would break early — in `_parseAllLines` there's no caps, full parse, fine.

But in `_collectNewest`, `_parseCacheMisses++` only when the walk reaches the line — deliberate per comments.

7. Important correctness question: `_collectNewest`'s `missJByLine` built via `decodedJByOffset[lines[i].$1]`. If two lines have the same offset... can't. But `decoded` returns tuples (offset, text, weight) — presumably only successfully decoded lines. If a miss line failed to decode, j = null → missJByLine stays -1 → treated as torn. OK.

Wait — one real bug candidate: in `_collectNewest`, torn lines from cache (hit with null entry) set `torn[i] = true`. But in `_parseAllLines`, `results[i] = entry` where entry may be null (torn marker) — results stays null, correct skip.

8. Another: the reverse-walk early-break and cache misses: the walk breaks when caps hit, so lines not reached aren't stored (and not counted as misses). But their decode already happened upfront (`_decodeLines` for all misses). So a repeat scan re-decodes... wait no — repeat scan probes cache: unreached miss lines were never stored, so they're misses again, decode again. That matches old volume roughly. Fine.

So the whole reader already assumes append-only; the cache extends the same assumption from "resume offsets" to "parsed content". If the contract is already load-bearing elsewhere, this is consistent. But the *impact* differs: with append violation, old code would show the new content on re-read (self-healing), while cached code serves stale records indefinitely (until a shrink/same-size-mtime). Also re-store after eviction: line probed miss (not in cache), then... only inserted once per scan. Across concurrent scans possible. Minor.

Another: `_decodeLines` on misses list preserves offsets; `decodedJByOffset` maps offset→j. If two miss lines had the same offset — impossible.

Also `splitSessionParseBatches` receives texts with `firstLineNumber: base` where base = decoded.first.$1 = first miss offset. Batch line numbering is offset-based. `batchOfMiss[start + p]` where start = batch.firstLineNumber - base. OK.

Edge: `decoded.isEmpty` → batches empty; walk: every miss has missJByLine = -1 → torn store. But wait — if decoded is empty because all misses were... decoded empty only if all decode attempts failed/dropped (empty raws are excluded upfront via `raw.isEmpty` → torn without cache probe... hmm actually for `raw.isEmpty` the code sets `torn[i]=true; continue;` without probing/storing. An empty line at offset O: on a re-scan, `raw.isEmpty` check happens before probe → torn again without store. Consistent, cheap.)

Now the counter semantics: `_parseCacheMisses++` per reached miss in `_collectNewest`; plus `_parseCacheMisses += missIdx.length` in `_parseAllLines`. So a `readAround` that calls readForward (→_parseAllLines) + backward walk (→_collectNewest) counts misses in both. Tests presumably assert exact numbers; PR says "exactly 10 new misses". OK.

Potential issue: in `_parseAllLines`, `_parseCacheMisses += missIdx.length` counts misses for lines that fail to decode (never actually parsed) and lines whose record==null (stored as torn — legit miss). Old semantics "a miss means decode+parse work actually done" — decode-failed lines did cost decode work. Fine.

Now the timestamp/freshness: `_noteParseCacheStamp(info.size, info.mtimeMs)` in stat(). One concern: stat() is also called by external callers for chunk staleness (SessionChunk carries fileSize/fileMtimeMs). Same-size rewrite clears cache — but note WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended: does it ever rewrite same-size while the reader holds cache? The rule says same-size mtime move = rewrite → clear. OK.

Edge: **size grows, mtime changes, but the file was also rewritten at earlier offsets** (net growth + prefix rewrite in one save). Append-only contract violated → stale cache entries. The old code self-healed on re-read; the new one serves stale records until shrink/same-size event. How real is this? WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended appends; session files are append-only by design. If some other tool edits the file (compaction, crash recovery rewriting the tail...) — crash recovery usually truncates (shrink → cleared) or rewrites same-size (cleared). A rewrite that both changes prefix AND grows is exotic. I'll flag as IMPORTANT with the note that a conservative alternative is clearing on any mtime change (cost: cache invalidates on every append — that would defeat the purpose for live-tail... no wait, growth keeps entries by design since appends don't change old bytes). Could use (size, mtime) pair comparison: clear when mtime changed AND... can't distinguish append from rewrite via stat alone. So the append-only contract is necessary. It's documented in the PR. I'll raise it as IMPORTANT (documented assumption, self-healing lost) — or SUGGESTION? The reader's readForward resume already trusts append-only (resume offsets would be wrong after prefix rewrite anyway — actually no: resume reads bytes at offsets; if bytes changed, old code would return the NEW parsed records at those offsets — self-healing). The cache makes staleness sticky. I think IMPORTANT is fair, since it changes observable behavior under contract violation. But is the append-only contract actually guaranteed anywhere? The PR asserts it as "the ingestAppended rewrite rule" and "the same signal readForward resumes from". Given sessions are JSONL append logs written by this codebase's own storage, the contract holds. I'll flag it IMPORTANT-ish but leaning... Let me think about severity per rules: BLOCKING = bug/security/CI break. This isn't a bug under the stated contract. IMPORTANT = real maintainability/correctness issue. A sticky-stale cache under contract violation with a tiny detection gap (same-ms same-size rewrites) — I'll make it one IMPORTANT comment about the mtime-granularity hole + sticky staleness, recommending documenting the append-only precondition at the storage contract level or clearing on any mtime change for same-size... Actually the code DOES clear on same-size mtime change. The hole is only: (a) rewrite+net-growth (contract violation), (b) mtime granularity < rewrite interval (e.g., fs with 1s granularity or same-ms rewrites → same-size rewrite missed). (b) is real: if fs mtime resolution is 1s and ingestAppended does a same-size rewrite twice within one second, second rewrite undetected. But ingestAppended — does it rewrite same-size often? The clear rule exists precisely for it. If two same-size rewrites happen within one mtime tick, the cache from after the first rewrite survives the second → stale. Narrow but real. I'll fold this into one IMPORTANT.

Now the double-quote import: line 16 `import "dart:convert";`. Original single-quoted. Style inconsistency introduced. Check repo lint — analysis_options grep found no prefer_single_quotes. Still, every other import uses single quotes; this looks accidental. SUGGESTION.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config

- **Additions**: +814

- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Old `_collectNewest`: decoded ALL lines, split into batches, parsed batches newest-first, broke at caps. Parse volume = batches up to cap point.

New: decodes all misses upfront (utf8 decode — this is eager, not lazy), then walks newest-first parsing batches lazily. So utf8 decode volume for a capped tail read can now exceed the old volume? Old code also decoded all lines upfront (`_decodeLines(lines)` on all lines). Same. OK, no change.

`_parseCacheMisses` semantics: probe-free counting... fine.

Now one more check on correctness: `_collectNewest` line `if (raw.isEmpty) { torn[i] = true; continue; }` — old code: `_decodeLines` dropped empty lines, so they never became records. Same.

But wait — in `_collectNewest`, for cache-hit entries with entry != null, `resolved[i] = entry`. For torn hits, `torn[i] = true`. Then the walk: `var entry = resolved[i]; if (entry == null) { miss path }`. For a torn hit, torn[i]=true so `continue` at `if (torn[i]) continue;`. Good.

Subtle: in the miss path, `_parseCacheMisses++` happens even when `j < 0` (undecodable). Comment says "A miss that costs work: this is the only place a line turns into decode+parse (the probe above is counter-free)" — decode already happened upfront for all misses, but the counter counts only reached ones. The decode of unreached misses is not counted — consistent with "caps' parse volume" claim? It's about parse (jsonDecode), not utf8 decode. OK.

Now the stale-cache risk analysis (finding candidate #1):

`_noteParseCacheStamp`: clears only when size < stamp, or size == stamp && mtime changed. Grows keep. Risks:
1. Same-size rewrite where mtime granularity fails to observe a change (fs with coarse mtime, or rewrite within same mtime tick as the last stat). Then stale bytes served. Old code: no staleness possible. Probability: low but nonzero. Also `ingestAppended` — let me check what windowed_session_storage.ingestAppended does on same-size rewrite; it presumably writes then relies on mtime. Actually the reader clear rule mirrors the storage's own rule, and the storage itself would also be stale in that case (its window cache). So the risk is inherited, not new. Hmm.

2. Growth + prefix rewrite (contract violation): sticky staleness, no self-heal.

Both hinge on the append-only contract. The PR documents the contract. I'll rate this IMPORTANT (worth a comment) — it changes failure mode from self-healing to sticky-stale under contract violation, and mtime-granularity holes exist.

The impact is re-decode of junk lines only (rare), so SUGGESTION is fair. I'll skip or fold into a suggestion. Actually let me not overload; skip it — it self-corrects via eviction.

Docs say "parseCacheEntries: 0 disables (pre-#1498 behavior)". But note: with entries disabled, `_parseCacheMisses` still counts (in _collectNewest reached-miss increments, and _parseAllLines adds missIdx.length) — counters keep incrementing even when disabled, and `parseCacheHitCount` stays 0. Harmless. Skip.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config

- **Additions**: +814

- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:09:08Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1498

## Root cause (measured, not assumed)
The profile's `parseSessionEntryLine` 1.2ms/call × 104,606 calls was dominated by **re-parsing**: every backward doubling pass, repeat `jumpToOffset`/`readAround` (TUI scroll), and capped `readForward` re-decoded lines already materialized this open. Repro bench (10k-line / 27.9MB synthetic session, 200-record windows, inline parse):

| scenario | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 30× `readAround` jumps, first batch | 166ms | 79ms (doubling-pass overlap deduped) |
| same jumps, warm (the scroll pattern) | 150ms | **50ms (3.0x)** — 51,459 cache hits |
| warm per jump | ~5.0ms | **~1.7ms** (issue bar: <50ms cache-hit) |
| open `readTail` misses (10k-line fixture) | 200 records + re-parses per pass | exactly 200 (each line parsed once) |

Per-line `parseSessionEntryLine` is **unchanged by design**: micro-split shows jsonDecode = 78% / record build = 16% of a 500×4KB batch — the VM decoder is already near-peak, so the honest algorithmic fix was the multiplicative re-parse, not the single call. Per-kind bench shipped in `bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart` (`dart bench/issue_1498_parse_bench.dart`); per-kind numbers move within noise, as expected.

## Delivered
- `SessionChunkReader` parsed-line cache keyed **(offset, byteLength, shallow)** — `_collectNewest` and `_parseAllLines` probe before any utf8-decode/jsonDecode; batch parsing in `_collectNewest` stays lazy so the caps' parse volume matches the uncached walk (a repeat scan adds **zero** misses).
- **Byte-compat**: the `shallow` flag is part of the key — the resume walk's header-only giant customs can never serve a full-fidelity read and vice versa; records are immutable and returned as parsed; torn-line quarantine, JSONL format, record shapes and IO read patterns unchanged.
- **Freshness** on the storage's own signals, re-validated at every `stat()`: growth keeps entries (append-only contract), shrink or same-size mtime move clears (the `ingestAppended` rewrite rule).
- **Bounded**: 4096 entries / 32MiB raw-line bytes, FIFO eviction, lines >4MiB never cached; `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables (pre-#1498 behavior).
- **Instrumentation** (the `locatePassCount` precedent): `parseCacheHitCount`/`parseCacheMissCount`/`parseCacheEntryCount`.
- **Regression guards** (`test/session/session_parse_cache_test.dart`, 14 tests): repeat-window splice with identical records, capped re-forward, append keeps prefix (exactly 10 new misses), completed-torn-line re-parse, shrink + same-size-rewrite invalidation, shallow/full key separation, entry/byte caps, disable switch, torn/foreign junk skip — plus the bounded time guard: `jumpToOffset` ×5 on a synthetic 10k-line session under a generous 5s wall (measured ~10ms; the mechanism itself is pinned by the counters, not the clock).

## Not done (deliberate)
- Byte-range read dedup (issue item 3's IO half): warm jump cost is now byte-copy-bound (~1.7ms/jump, page-cache reads), 30x under the acceptance bar — not worth the added invalidation surface.
- Lazy/index-only parse (item 4, marked optional in the issue): changes observable record shapes; unnecessary once re-parses are deduped.

## Tests
- `dart analyze` clean on touched files (repo-wide run shows only pre-existing infos in unrelated files).
- `test/session/`: 320 passed (306 pre-existing + 14 new), incl. windowed property tests and structured-resume equivalence. Integration trajectory gates (`perf_open_gate_test` etc.) not runnable on this host (no /tmp write for fixtures) — left for CI.

## Automated Code Review — APPROVE

**Summary**: Well-executed, measured perf fix for #1498 — the (offset, byteLength, shallow) parse cache is correctly keyed, bounded, freshness-revalidated at every `stat()`, and guarded by 14 focused regression tests (all pass locally; `dart analyze` clean; full `test/session/` suite 320/320).

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md` — cache staleness window: append-only contract + mtime-granularity hole makes same-size rewrites sticky-stale where the old code self-healed.
- 💡 `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md` — `_parseAllLines` never caches decode-failed misses as torn (inconsistent with `_collectNewest`): junk lines re-decode on every full scan and inflate `parseCacheMissCount` forever.
- 💡 `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md` — `import "dart:convert"` switched to double quotes (style regression).
- 💡 `outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md` — `parseCacheBytes: 0` semantics (unlimited budget) undocumented and asymmetric with `parseCacheEntries: 0` (disables).

**Next Steps**:
1. Address the staleness-window note (document the contract or tighten invalidation) before a future session file is ever rewritten by an external tool.
2. Optionally align the two torn-store paths and restore the single-quote import.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Staleness window — append-only contract + mtime granularity make rewrites sticky-stale**

`_noteParseCacheStamp` keeps all entries whenever the file grew and only clears on observed shrink or observed same-size mtime move. Two holes follow:

1. **Unobserved same-size rewrite.** The clear on `size == stamp && mtimeMs != stampMtime` only fires if the mtime actually changed between two `stat()` calls. If a same-size rewrite lands inside the same mtime tick as the previous stat (filesystems with 1s granularity, or two quick `ingestAppended` rewrites in one millisecond), the cache keeps entries whose bytes were overwritten and serves stale records indefinitely — while the pre-#1498 code re-read bytes on every scan and self-healed. This matters precisely for the rewrite path the comment names (`WindowedSessionStorage.ingestAppended`), where mtime is the *only* invalidation signal.

2. **Growth + prefix rewrite (contract violation).** Any tool that rewrites earlier bytes while the file net-grows (compaction, hand-edited JSONL) leaves every old entry sticky-stale; `readForward`'s resume offsets survive that, but cached parsed content does not self-heal.

Suggestions:
- State the append-only precondition explicitly in the class doc (it is currently implied), so future writers know a prefix rewrite must shrink or touch mtime.
- Consider clearing on *any* mtime change when `size == stamp`, and additionally when `size > stamp && mtimeMs == stampMtime` (an append that didn't move mtime is indistinguishable from an in-place rewrite at this granularity) — or accept and document the residual risk, since `WindowedSessionStorage`'s own window cache inherits the same signal.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `_parseAllLines` never caches decode-failed misses as torn**

In `_collectNewest` a miss whose bytes fail `_decodeLines` is remembered via `_parseCacheStoreTorn` (`j < 0` branch), so a re-visited window skips the decode attempt. The same line in `_parseAllLines` silently falls out: misses absent from `decoded` (strict-UTF8 failures) are never stored, so every full scan (`readTail`/`readForward`/`readBlockBefore`) re-decodes them, and `_parseCacheMisses += missIdx.length` keeps counting them on every pass — which also means the "a repeat scan adds zero misses" property the counters pin does not actually hold for junk lines on the full-parse path.

Fix is a few lines: after building `lineIdxByOffset`, iterate `missIdx` and `_parseCacheStoreTorn` the offsets missing from it (mirroring `_collectNewest`).

💡 **SUGGESTION: double-quoted import**

The diff changes `import 'dart:convert';` to `import "dart:convert";` — every other import in this file (and the repo convention) uses single quotes, and the change is unrelated to #1498. Looks accidental; please revert to `import 'dart:convert';`.

💡 **SUGGESTION: document `parseCacheBytes: 0` semantics**

`_evictParseCache` only applies the byte budget when `parseCacheBytes > 0`, so `0` means "no byte budget" (entry cap still applies) — while `parseCacheEntries: 0` disables the cache entirely. The constructor doc only describes the `parseCacheEntries: 0` case. One line on the field doc (`/// 0 means no byte budget; combined with [parseCacheEntries] 0 it fully disables the cache.`) removes the ambiguity for the next reader.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
